items.title: Section: The Four Formless Absorptions — Dissolving Space, Then Consciousness, Then Everything

items.zh: 以於虛空起勝解故，所有青、黃、赤、白等相應顯色想，由不顯現故，及厭離欲故，皆能超越，是故說言：色想出過故。由不顯現、超越彼想以為因故，所有種種眾多品類，因諸顯色和合積集有障礙想皆得除遣，是故說言：有對想滅沒故。由遠離彼想以為因故，所有於彼種種聚中差別想轉，謂飲、食、瓶、衣、乘、莊嚴具、城、舍、軍、園、山、林等想，於是一切不作意轉，是故說言：種種想不作意故。除遣如是有色、有對種種想已，起無邊相虛空勝解，是故說言：入無邊空。
items.en: Because one gives rise to confident understanding of empty space, every perception of visible colour associated with it — blue, yellow, red, white, and the rest — is entirely transcended, since it no longer appears at all and since one is repelled by it and free of desire for it; for this reason it is said: because perception of form is transcended … having dispelled every such perception of form, of resistance, and of manifold variety, one gives rise to a boundless perception, confident understanding of empty space itself; for this reason it is said: one enters boundless space.

items.zh: 由已超過近分加行究竟作意，入上根本加行究竟果作意定，是故說言：空無邊處具足安住。當知此中，依於近分，乃至未入上根本定，唯緣虛空。若已得入上根本定，亦緣虛空，亦緣自地所有諸蘊。又近分中，亦緣下地所有諸蘊。復次，
若由此識，於無邊空發起勝解，當知此識無邊空相勝解相應。若有欲入識無邊處，先捨虛空無邊處想，即於彼識，次起無邊行相勝解。爾時超過近分、根本空無邊處，是故說言：超過一切空無邊處，入無邊識。
items.en: Since it is by means of this very consciousness that confident understanding of boundless space first arose … one now, with respect to that same consciousness, gives rise next to confident understanding of its boundless aspect instead. At that time one transcends both the approach to and the root absorption of infinite space, and for this reason it is said: transcending every stage of infinite space, one enters infinite consciousness.

items.zh: 由彼超過識無邊處所有近分，乃至加行究竟作意，入上根本加行究竟果作意定，是故說言：識無邊處具足安住。復次，
從識無邊處求上進時，離其識外更求餘境，都無所得。謂諸所有或色、非色相應境性。彼求境界無所得時，超過近分及以根本識無邊處，發起都無餘境勝解，此則名為於無所有假想勝解。
items.en: When, striving to advance beyond infinite consciousness, one seeks some further object apart from that very consciousness, one finds nothing at all to be gained … when the search for an object yields nothing to be gained, one transcends both the approach to and the root absorption of infinite consciousness, giving rise to confident understanding that no further object whatsoever remains — this is called the imagined confident understanding of nothingness.

items.zh: 即於如是假想勝解多修習故，便能超過無所有處一切近分，乃至加行究竟作意，入彼根本加行究竟果作意定，是故說言：超過一切識無邊處，無少所有無所有處具足安住。復次，從無所有處求上進時，
由於無所有處想起麁想故，便能棄捨無所有處想。由是因緣，先入無所有處定時，超過一切有所有想，今復超過無所有想。是故說言：非有想，謂或有所有想，或無所有想；非無想，謂非如無想及滅盡定，一切諸想皆悉滅盡。唯有微細想，緣無相境轉，是故說言：非想非非想。
items.en: Because one gives rise to a perception of coarseness with respect to the perception of nothingness itself, one becomes able to relinquish even that perception of nothingness … "not having perception" means having neither perception of something nor perception of nothing; "not lacking perception" means it is unlike the attainment of no-perception or the attainment of cessation, in which every perception without exception has ceased … only a most subtle perception remains, operating with respect to a signless object — for this reason it is said: neither perception nor non-perception.

items.zh: 即於此處起勝解時，超過一切近分、根本無所有處，及非想非非想處近分，乃至加行究竟作意，入彼根本加行究竟果作意定，是故說言：超過一切無所有處。於非想非非想處具足安住。復次，此中入靜慮定時，其身相狀如處室中；入無色定時，其身相狀如處虛空。當知此中，由奢摩他相，安住上捨，勤修加行。復次，依靜慮等，當知能入二無心定。一者、無想定，二者、滅盡定。

blocks.text: The four formless attainments: space, consciousness, nothingness, and neither perception nor non-perception. Two short passages are untranslated.

"Because one gives rise to confident understanding of empty space, every perception of visible colour (blue, yellow, red, white) is transcended, since it no longer appears and one is free of desire for it." So one "transcends the perception of form", "the perception of resistance ceases", and "one does not attend to perceptions of diversity". Then "a boundless perception of empty space".
"It is by this very consciousness that the understanding of boundless space arose." So one turns to that consciousness, and gives rise to confident understanding of its boundlessness.
"Seeking some further object apart from that consciousness, one finds nothing at all to be gained." That is the sphere of nothingness.

"Seeing coarseness even in the perception of nothingness, one relinquishes it." What remains is "having neither perception of something nor perception of nothing": "only a most subtle perception, operating on a signless object". Master Cháng Bǎi: a little subtle perception remains, but there is no verbal, discursive thought; hence "neither perception nor non-perception".
These states are the summit of the mundane path, and the treatise has already warned (Day 235) that they are not liberation: Udraka reached the highest and was reborn there, afflictions intact.

quiz.q: Infinite space: "because perception of form is transcended" — the English gives one reason. What do the lectures say?
options: Miào Jìng: besides non-appearance, a second reason — detachment; Cháng Bǎi: this space isn't prajñā emptiness but contaminated
quiz.why: "Is entirely transcended; for this reason it is said: because perception of form is transcended." Venerable Miào Jìng: non-appearance is one thing; the second is "because of detachment from desire." Master Cháng Bǎi: this space isn't the space of "form is emptiness" — not prajñā's emptiness but contaminated space. The English omits the detachment reason.

quiz.q: "Confident understanding of boundless space — entering boundless space." Does the body still feel present in the approach stage, according to Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: the object is vast space, but the body still feels present — lower aggregates still taken
quiz.why: "One gives rise to a boundless perception, confident understanding of empty space itself; for this reason it is said: one enters boundless space." Master Cháng Bǎi: the object is only a vast expanse of space, yet the body still feels present, because one also takes the lower stage's aggregates as object.

quiz.q: Transcending infinite space, one enters infinite consciousness. What does Venerable Miào Jìng say one sees in infinite space's root absorption?
options: no body, but still feeling, perception, formations, consciousness
quiz.why: "At that time one transcends both the approach to and the root absorption of infinite space; for this reason it is said: transcending every stage of infinite space, one enters infinite consciousness." Venerable Miào Jìng: at this time he doesn't see himself as having a body; he sees he still has the four aggregates of feeling, perception, formations, consciousness.

quiz.q: Why "neither perception nor non-perception," according to Master Cháng Bǎi?
options: a most subtle perception remains, on a signless object, without verbal thought
quiz.why: "Only a most subtle perception remains, operating with respect to a signless object — for this reason it is said: neither perception nor non-perception." Master Cháng Bǎi: a little subtle perception remains, operating on a signless object; there's no verbal discursive thought — hence "neither perception nor non-perception."

quiz.q: In the formless absorptions, seeking beyond, "nothing is found." What does Venerable Miào Jìng say they lean towards?
options: calm — insight is scant, practically none
quiz.why: "When, striving to advance beyond infinite consciousness, one seeks some further object apart from that very consciousness, one finds nothing at all to be gained." Venerable Miào Jìng: the four formless absorptions lean towards calm; insight is very, very little — practically none.
